result.notes:
3785 distinct crafted arguments, each byte-compared against a Rust re-implementation of the model (full 12-line stdout via `cmp`-equivalent Vec<u8> equality, plus exit status and empty-stderr checks). Whole suite was run twice with identical results (7570 total invocations). ZERO divergences on any line.

Coverage for the is_valid_domain / length lens:
- Exhaustive length sweep 0..=400 across 4 content generators (all-'a'; "a." alternating; high bytes 0x80+i; a 15-byte cycle mixing ASCII upper/lower, '.', '-', 2/3/4-byte UTF-8) = 1604 probes. Boundary is exactly len>=1 && len<=255 in every generator.
- Every filler byte value 0x01..0xFF repeated to exactly 255 (valid) and 256 (invalid) = 510 probes. No byte value shifts the boundary.
- Shapes at len 252..258: all-dots, all-spaces, all-newlines, all-hyphens, all-0xFF, all-0x80, all-0x01, all-0xBF, leading dot, trailing dot, "a." alternating, "-.": alternating, empty-label "a..b" patterns, 3/4/5 x 63-byte labels (+0..2 extra), 1-3 x 64-byte labels, single labels of 64/65/100/200/250/251/252 + ".com", "ab." pattern + ".com". All follow pure byte length.
- Multibyte straddle: 126/127/128/129 x C3A9; 84/85/86 x E282AC; 62/63/64/65 x F09F9880; plus each padded with 1-4 ASCII bytes to land on 255/256; truncated sequences at the boundary (254a+C3, 253a+E282, 252a+F09F98 and their +1 counterparts); overlong C080, surrogate EDA080, out-of-range F4908080. Length is BYTES, never codepoints, and invalid UTF-8 argv is handled identically.
- No trimming/normalizing before the length test: 255a+space, +2sp, +tab, +\n, +\r, +'.', +'..', space+255a are all 256+ bytes and all report invalid (a trailing-dot- or whitespace-stripping implementation would have said valid).
- 1400 randomized fuzz strings (lengths biased 240-262, plus 0-600) over three alphabets including all 255 non-NUL bytes.
- Over-long inputs change ONLY line 5: verified at 259,260,300,511,512,1000,1023,4096,8192,32768,65535,65536,100000,131070,131071 bytes with uppercase/dots/high-bytes/trailing-dot content. normalize (line 10), extract_tld (line 11) and count_labels (line 12) stay correct on over-long inputs (e.g. 100000 dots -> tld "" and 100001 labels; huge uppercase input is still fully lowercased). Lines 1-4 also still echo the full over-long string.
- 131071 bytes is the hard ceiling for a single argv entry on this platform (execve MAX_ARG_STRLEN); anything larger fails to spawn and cannot be tested.
- Extra args are ignored even when huge (argv[2] of 100000 bytes) and even when argv[1] is empty; determinism confirmed by 12x repeats of the 255/256 pair (no uninitialized-memory variance).
- Locale cannot perturb to_lower: tested LC_ALL=C, C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8, de_DE.ISO-8859-1, LANG=tr_TR.UTF-8, LC_CTYPE=en_US.ISO-8859-1 with Latin-1 uppercase bytes (0xC0..0xDE) and with "ABCIiJ" content. Output identical; bytes >= 0x80 are never case-mapped and 'I' never becomes a dotless i.

Ground truth cross-check (read-only disassembly of /workspace/dataset/test12_executable, consistent with every probe):
- idna::is_valid_domain: `!empty() && length() <= 0xff` (single `cmp $0xff,%rax; ja`). No charset, label, hyphen or dot rules exist in the function at all.
- idna::is_valid_label: `!empty() && length() <= 0x3f` — so the real rule is 1..=63 bytes. test12 only ever passes "testlabel", so line 6 is always "1"; a port of this test only needs the constant, but a port of the header should implement 1..=63.
- idna::is_ascii_domain loops with `cmpb $0x0; jns` i.e. signed char >= 0, exactly "every byte < 0x80"; is_idn_domain is its complement.
- idna::extract_tld: `find_last_of('.')`; if npos return the whole string else `substr(pos+1)`. No lowercasing.
- idna::count_labels: counts '.' bytes into an `int`, returns count+1.
- idna::to_lower: copies the string then `std::transform(..., ::tolower)` (int(*)(int)) — plain C `tolower` in the never-changed "C" locale, so ASCII-only mapping; chars are signed so bytes >= 0x80 arrive as negative ints and come back unchanged.
- idna::punycode_encode: `"xn--" + s`. idna::punycode_decode / to_unicode: `find("xn--") == 0` then `substr(4)`, else copy — one whole-string prefix strip, confirming no per-label and no real punycode.
- The library also exports unused-by-this-test symbols a full port may want to know about: split_labels, join_labels, sanitize_domain, has_invalid_chars (rejects the set including ' ', '@', '#', '$', '%', '^', '&', '*'), to_ascii_2003/2008, to_unicode_2003/2008, batch_to_ascii, set_strict_mode, get_last_error, clear_errors, get_max_label_length() = 63, get_min_label_length() = 1. None of these affect test12's 12 output lines.

No divergences found. 206 probes were full byte-for-byte diffs of the binary's stdout against a Rust reimplementation of the model (/tmp/model.rs, built with rustc, reading argv as raw bytes via OsStrExt); ~150 further process-level checks covered stdout/stderr/stdin/env/cwd/determinism. Every probe also asserted exit==0, stderr empty, and (for newline-free args) exactly 12 lines with a trailing 0x0a.

/workspace/dataset/test12.cpp is present and confirms the assumed main(): domain defaults to "multi.level.domain.name.test", is replaced by argv[1] when argc>1, and result1..result12 are computed and streamed in order with std::endl. Nothing else reads argv or the environment.

ARGV CONTRACT — all confirmed:
- Zero args: output byte-identical to passing the default explicitly (both 178 bytes, exactly 12 lines, no trailing bytes beyond the final newline).
- argc==0 (raw execv with an empty argv vector, via /tmp/execv_probe.rs — not reachable from bash) also yields the default output. `argc > 1` is the only gate.
- argv[2..] fully ignored: verified with 2, 3, 4, 201, and 20001 args, and with extras that were empty, 5 KB/1 MB long, newline-laden, non-UTF-8 (\xff\xfe\x80), "xn--"-prefixed, or equal to the default string. An invariance matrix (7 argv[1] values x {0,1,2,3 extra args}) produced byte-identical output in all 28 combinations.
- Empty argv[1] is honored as the domain, NOT treated as absent: line5=0, line12=1, lines 2/4/10/11 empty, lines 1/3 = "xn--". Still true when argv[2] is a valid domain ("" "second.com" -> line10 empty, line5=0), so there is no fallback-to-next-arg or fallback-to-default behavior.
- Args starting with '-'/'--' are plain domains, never flags: -h, --help, -?, /?, --, ---, -----, -0, --=, -abc, --version, --domain=example.com, -xn--abc etc. all flow straight into the library (e.g. "--help" -> line1 "xn----help", line11 "--help", line12 1). No getopt, no usage text, no early exit.
- argv[0] is irrelevant: tested via `exec -a` with names "weirdname0", "", "example.com", "-h", "--help", and one containing a newline; argument indexing never shifts.

EXIT/STDERR: exit status was 0 in every one of the ~360 runs (including a 30-input sweep with shell-metacharacter, format-specifier, and path-traversal-looking args). stderr was empty in every run, including with stdout closed (`>&-`), where the failed writes are silently swallowed and exit is still 0. stdin is never read (data piped in remains available to a following `cat`); closing stdin changes nothing. Output is identical to a file, to a pipe, and to /dev/null. cwd (/ vs /tmp vs the dataset dir) and `env -i` make no difference. 50 repeat runs of one input were bit-identical (no randomness/uninitialized reads).

LOCALE: LC_ALL/LANG/LC_CTYPE set to C, POSIX, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8, de_DE.ISO-8859-1 all produce identical bytes for "MIXED.Café.COM" — to_lower is not locale-sensitive (no Turkish-I behavior), reinforcing the pure byte-wise ASCII model.

ONE EXEC-TIME ARTIFACT (not a program divergence, but relevant to a port's test harness): a single argument of 131072 bytes or more cannot be exec'd at all — the kernel's MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32*PAGE_SIZE) makes execve fail with E2BIG, bash reports "Argument list too long" and exits 126, and the binary never runs. 131071 bytes works fine. The Rust model binary fails identically at the same boundary, so this is environmental, not behavioral. My first attempt at 1 MB/2 MB args tripped this; those 4 probes were re-run under the limit (130000 and 131000 bytes, with 'a', 'A', '.', and \xff fill) and all matched the model.

PORTING SUBTLETY (outside the 12-line stdout contract, so not scored as a divergence): with stdout closed the C++ binary exits 0 silently. A naive Rust port using println!/unwrap would panic and exit 101 there; the same applies to SIGPIPE (C++ dies on signal 13, Rust ignores SIGPIPE and would surface EPIPE). I could not trigger SIGPIPE naturally because the 178-byte output fits in a pipe buffer — `| head -c 3` returned 0 for both binaries.

Key files: /workspace/dataset/test12.cpp (the harness main, matches the model), /workspace/dataset/test12_executable (reference binary), /tmp/model.rs + /tmp/model (byte-exact model predictor), /tmp/harness.sh (differential probe driver), /tmp/execv_probe.rs (argc==0 prober).

NO DIVERGENCES FOUND. The model is exactly correct for all 12 output lines. Confirmed two independent ways: (A) 7628 differential probes comparing the real binary's stdout byte-for-byte (cmp) against a Rust reimplementation of the model; (B) reading the actual machine code with objdump, which matches the model instruction-for-instruction.

PROBE BREAKDOWN: 1870 curated bash probes (xn--/XN--/Xn--/xN-- case variants, xn-/xn---/xn----/xn-----, exactly "xn--", prefix at start/middle/end, repeated "xn--xn--xn--", real punycode bodies, dot-only strings from 1 to 99999 dots, trailing/leading dots, empty last label, deep nesting to 1000 labels, length boundaries 0..1024 plus 130000/131060 bytes, control chars, invalid UTF-8); 3700 random-byte fuzz iterations across 4 alphabets (xn--/dot-heavy ASCII, full 0x01-0xFF, high-byte-heavy, printable ASCII) spawned via execve so argv carries arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes; 2040 exhaustive single-byte probes placing every byte value 0x01-0xFF in 8 structural positions (bare, after "xn--", before "xn--", as TLD, as label before empty TLD, as middle label, and inside the prefix region as "xn?--q" and "x?--q"); 18 locale probes. Every probe also asserted exit status 0, empty stderr, and a trailing 0x0a byte. Zero mismatches.

DISASSEMBLY CONFIRMATION (addresses in /workspace/dataset/test12_executable):
- to_ascii @0x402843: copies the string, std::transform(begin,end,begin,::tolower), then std::operator+("xn--", lowered). Literal "xn--" at 0x405036.
- to_unicode @0x4028f1 and punycode_decode @0x402983 are byte-identical logic: s.find("xn--", 0) == 0 ? s.substr(4, npos) : s. One strip, exactly 4 bytes, whole-string, never per-label.
- punycode_encode @0x402958: operator+("xn--", s), no lowercasing.
- is_valid_domain @0x4029ea: !empty() && length() <= 255 (cmp $0xff / ja).
- is_ascii_domain @0x402a6a: per-char `cmpb $0 / jns`, i.e. signed char >= 0, equivalent to byte < 0x80. is_idn_domain @0x402ae9 is literally is_ascii_domain XOR 1.
- to_lower @0x402ceb: std::transform(..., ::tolower) on a copy. normalize @0x402d77 just calls to_lower, nothing else.
- extract_tld @0x40310c: find_last_of('.', npos); if npos return copy of domain else substr(pos+1, npos). No lowercasing anywhere.
- count_labels @0x403480: int count = 0; for each char if (c=='.') count++; return count + 1.

WORTH KNOWING FOR THE PORT:
1. is_valid_label is NOT unobservable in the library, only in this test program. At 0x402a2b it is `!l.empty() && l.length() <= 63` (cmp $0x3f / ja). The test only passes "testlabel" (9 bytes) so line 6 is always "1", but a faithful port should implement !l.is_empty() && l.len() <= 63.
2. to_lower is locale-INDEPENDENT in practice: it calls glibc ::tolower via PLT, but the program never calls setlocale(), so the "C" locale is always active. stdout was byte-identical under LC_ALL = C, POSIX, de_DE.iso88591, tr_TR.utf8, tr_TR.iso88599, en_US.utf8 with inputs 0xC9 0xD6 0xDC, "ISTANBUL", and "I U+0130 i". Plain b'A'..=b'Z' -> +32 is correct; no Turkish-I or Latin-1 case mapping.
3. char is signed on x86-64 and is sign-extended into ::tolower for bytes >= 0x80, but the C-locale table is identity there, so high bytes pass through unchanged (confirmed by the 2040-probe byte sweep).
4. count_labels returns `int`. Overflow needs 2^31 dots; Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN caps one argv entry at 131072 bytes, so it is unreachable. 99999 dots -> 100000 matched exactly.
5. Output framing held universally: 12 std::endl-terminated fields, exit 0, empty stderr. Inputs containing 0x0a yield more than 12 physical lines yet still matched byte-for-byte, so do not hardcode a 12-line assumption in a port's test harness.
6. Extra args beyond argv[1] are ignored (verified with 2 and 3 args, including empty argv[1] followed by non-empty argv[2]).
7. /workspace/dataset/test12.cpp is present and gives the exact call sequence, including that line 9 is the constant to_lower("MIXEDCase") -> "mixedcase", independent of input.
8. The library exports many unused symbols (split_labels, join_labels, sanitize_domain, to_ascii_2003/2008, to_unicode_2003/2008, has_invalid_chars, is_reserved_label, get_max_label_length, get_min_label_length, batch_to_ascii, batch_to_unicode, convert_encoding, set_strict_mode, set_use_std3_ascii_rules, set_transitional_processing, set_verify_dns_length, get_last_error, clear_errors). None are reachable from test12.cpp, so none can affect the 12 outputs.

Artifacts, all under /tmp (nothing in /workspace or /output was modified): /tmp/model.rs (model reimplementation), /tmp/fuzz.rs (random-byte differential fuzzer), /tmp/sweep.rs (exhaustive single-byte structural sweep), /tmp/h2.sh (bash differential harness), /tmp/batchA.sh .. /tmp/batchE.sh (curated probe batches).
